title: Redwood Discovery - Model Selection - Kelp Analytics
next_steps: Send tailored pricing comparison (hosted vs dedicated) - Miles to own
Share SOC 2 & network architecture + KMS docs - Priya to share
Schedule 60-min benchmark session with 50k-token context and multilingual tests - Marcelo/Dana to confirm date
action_items: Miles: Send pricing + hosted vs dedicated cost model (due 2027-09-10)
Priya: Share SOC2, SAML/SSO docs, VPC deploy checklist (due 2027-09-09)
Marcelo: Provide sample prompt sets and target latency SLOs (due 2027-09-12)
Lina: Confirm internal compliance reviewers for private deployment (due 2027-09-13)
summary: Discovery call focused on open model selection and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Kelp Analytics needs long context (document ingestion up to 50k tokens), strong multilingual support, and tool-calling for data connectors. Security and data residency are gating. Next steps: pricing, security docs, and benchmarking session.
transcript:
[00:00] Miles: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:06] Dana: Hey, Dana Cho, CTO at Kelp Analytics. We do document summarization & insights for maritime supply chain, big multi-language docs.
[00:12] Marcelo: Marcelo Ruiz, lead ML; we're evaluating models for production inference, latency and cost are both big.
[00:18] Lina: Lina Park, SRE, I'll be focused on VPC, networking, and compliance bits.
[00:24] Miles: Great. I'm Miles, AE, and with me is Priya Shah, our solutions engineer.
[00:30] Priya: Hi all. Quick agenda: understand your workload (context length, multilingual), discuss open model options and tradeoffs, and deployment choices - hosted, dedicated, private.
[01:05] Dana: High level: we process technical manuals and incident logs in English, Mandarin, Spanish, sometimes Arabic. Need to do callouts across multiple docs - sometimes need 30k-50k token windows to reason.
[01:24] Marcelo: Yeah, we also need tool-calling to hit our connectors (internal DBs, a document store) and to call our verification services.
[01:33] Priya: Cool - that's helpful. On context: Redwood supports model variants with long-context and we also do KV-cache and prefix caching to make repeated snippets cheaper. For 50k tokens, we generally look at the larger open models or sharded context approaches.
[01:52] Marcelo: When you say "larger open models" - which ones are you running on hosted? We care about multiling and tool support.
[02:01] Priya: On hosted we currently have a catalog: Llama2 variants earlier, but more recent are Mistral / RedStone-family, and we also offer customer-configurable open checkpoints (e.g., Orca/RedWAVE style models) - hopeful that's not too jargon-y, sorry. For long context we recommend models with native long-context kernels or models we run with sequence chunking and KV cache.
[02:28] Dana: Is GPT-style tool calling supported? We've built tooling around function-calls.
[02:34] Priya: Yes, we support structured tool-calling and function-like APIs. On-hosted that's available, and in Dedicated/Private as well - function/schema-based calls. Some older open checkpoints may need adapters so there can be minor engineering work.
[02:50] Miles: A couple of commercial tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to get started (self-serve), cost is usage-based, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit-cost at scale but requires committed capacity, Private is for VPC/on-prem with highest control - usually chosen for strict data residency or regulated workloads.
[03:14] Lina: For Private, how does key management work? We have to use our HSM for keys.
[03:19] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS / HSM and can run a private control plane; the on-prem package supports HSM or customer KMS. Audit logs and per-token tracing are available.
[03:30] Marcelo: Latency - if we go with 50k context and tool-calls, do you see 1s per turn? 2s? We need sub-3s for short interactions, but long-batch summarizations can be higher.
[03:43] Priya: For 50k it's workload-dependent - streaming isn't usually used for full 50k synthesis; for chunked summarization pipelines, throughput is tuned. On Dedicated we can hit lower p99 latencies for medium seq lengths. For very long context the main cost is memory and kernel selection - we use quantized kernels and fused attention to reduce memory. Expect higher latency than short 2k prompts.
[04:10] Dana: Cost estimate please, high level. We have a small team and are cost-sensitive.
[04:15] Miles: We'll send tailored pricing, but to set expectation: hosted per-token for a 50k window is higher; Dedicated monthly reserved can be cheaper if you commit to throughput. We can run a pilot to measure unit costs.
[04:29] Marcelo: How about multilingual fidelity? Are models fine-tuned for Mandarin/Arabic?
[04:34] Priya: Some open models have good multilingual coverage; others are English-first. We typically recommend a mix: a multilingual base model for general reasoning, and fine-tune or eval a second model on your language-specific corpora. We can help with evals and give automated regression alerts.
[04:55] Dana: Any customers in regulated environments? We have to show SOC 2 & ISO readiness to partners.
[04:59] Miles: Yes - we have enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private who require SOC 2 and ISO; Redwood itself has SOC 2 reports and can share compliance pack. Priya will share the docs.
[05:14] Lina: Networking specifics: do you allow egress restrictions, private link to S3, and custom VPC peering?
[05:19] Priya: Yes, Private deployment supports VPC peering, private link, and can lock down egress. For Hosted we offer VPC endpoints in some regions and strict controls on data retention.
[05:33] Marcelo: Tool-calling latency - if the model triggers a DB lookup and waits for response, do you recommend async patterns?
[05:40] Priya: Yes, async patterns and streaming function results are common. Also consider prefetching and cached metadata to avoid round trips for hot keys.
[05:52] Dana: Can you run benchmarks on our data? We want to test hallucination rates when asked to reconcile ship manifests across multiple docs.
[05:58] Miles: Absolutely - typical next step is a benchmark session where you share sample prompts and we run hosted or dedicated tests, including hallucination/precision metrics.
[06:09] Marcelo: About model ops - how do we pin versions and roll back if quality regresses after a model update?
[06:15] Priya: Version pinning is supported - per-route model pins, canary rollouts, A/B, automatic fallback to older pinned variants. We also provide eval hooks tied to prompt sets to trigger alerts.
[06:30] Dana: Any constraints on model size for Dedicated? We have budgets for 8xA100-equivalent GPUs but might want more.
[06:36] Miles: Dedicated can be sized, and we'll give throughput estimates based on GPU type and model. For really large models you can also use sharded execution; we'll model VM/GPU needs in the proposal.
[06:52] Marcelo: Curious about quantization - do you support int8 or 4-bit for your higher perf paths?
[06:58] Priya: Yes, we support quantized execution paths - int8/4-bit depending on model compatibility. Performance varies; our optimizer chooses kernels at runtime. Sometimes there's a small quality delta, we surface that in recommendations.
[07:16] Lina: On telemetry - what's retained? We need to limit PII.
[07:20] Priya: By default we retain request metadata for observability and cost breakdowns; payload retention is configurable and can be turned off or routed to customer-managed storage for Private. We also support redaction and token-level hashing for PII-sensitive fields.
[07:38] Dana: Who would be our primary Redwood contacts during a pilot?
[07:41] Miles: I'll lead commercial and pilot coordination, Priya will handle the technical benching and SE work; we'll loop in a CSM if you move to Dedicated.
[07:52] Marcelo: For the benchmarking - can you run a 50k-context end-to-end test with multilingual prompts and tool-calls? That's our top priority.
[07:59] Priya: Yes, we'll need sample data and expected outputs. For long contexts, we might do engineered chunking + retrieval steps; we'll show both native long-context vs chunking tradeoffs.
[08:12] Dana: Any gotchas with our compliance team if we pick Hosted first and then move to Private? They worry about data exfiltration and audit trails.
[08:20] Miles: That's common - we often start with hosted for dev and then migrate to Private for production. We document the controls and can keep audit trails and SSO integrations in both modes; Private gives the most control.
[08:31] Marcelo: Competitors - we've been talking to Anthropic and OpenAI; how do you compare?
[08:36] Miles: In short: we focus on inference economics and operational controls. Other vendors may have closed models with specific quality profiles; our differentiator is flexibility across deployment modes and observability. We'll include benchmarking comparisons if you like.
[08:50] Lina: Any SLA/uptime commitments on Dedicated?
[08:53] Miles: Yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts.
[08:58] Dana: Timeline: we want to be production-ready for core features in Q4 - about 3 months. Is that realistic?
[09:05] Miles: With a scoped pilot in two to four weeks and a dedicated runbook, Q4 is feasible. It depends on fine-tuning, compliance reviews, and procurement.
[09:15] Marcelo: Ok, a couple of technical clarifications: do you support server-side function execution (so model returns a call token and Redwood executes out-of-band)?
[09:24] Priya: We support both patterns: model-driven calls and server-executed adapters. You can author function schemas and choose execution mode.
[09:31] Dana: Great. Any pricing model for function calls?
[09:34] Miles: Function calls are included in the request billing model; heavy external calls may incur additional infra cost - we'll call that out in pricing.
[09:43] Lina: Security: can Redwood meet our partner's data residency needs in EU and APAC?
[09:48] Priya: Yes - Hosted has regional endpoints, and Private can be deployed in-region. We can also do dedicated capacity in a given region.
[09:58] Marcelo: For evaluation, we'll give a dataset and a set of target metrics (latency, token cost, hallucination rate) - would Redwood be OK to run that and share raw logs?
[10:06] Miles: Yes, with an NDA or data agreement as needed. We can also run tests on synthetic or redacted data.
[10:15] Dana: Recap and next steps?
[10:18] Miles: Recap: you need long-context (~50k), multilingual + tool-calling, compliance (SOC2/KMS), cost sensitivity. Next steps we agreed: Miles to send pricing and proposal, Priya to share SOC2/network docs and schedule benchmark, Marcelo to share prompts and datasets, Lina to confirm compliance reviewers.
[10:37] Dana: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:40] Miles: Thanks folks - we'll follow up by end of week.
[10:45] End of recording
